Anthony, 2026-10-13: "Go with your recommendation on: which oh-my-pi ideas, (a) to (h), to keep." The recommendation was to keep (a) to (d), because they concern the seams between the harness and the graph, not features.

No new requirement was added. Each kept idea landed on a record that already existed, with a dated note:
- (a): evidence on dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set (31 tools against 197).
- (b): a clause on req:the-site-says-what-reflow2-is-and-is-not-as-a-partnership-in-plain-words (reflow2 is not an agent's private memory, and says what it holds that such memory does not).
- (c): clause (f) on req:the-mcp-surface-is-sized-for-tokens-per-task (a lesson rides the reply of the call that trips it).
- (d): emphasis on req:every-agent-working-a-design-is-its-own-claimant-subagents-included (parallel subagents are the harness default, and nothing delivers per-agent identity yet).

Recorded as considered, not chosen:
- (e) hash-anchored compare-and-swap edits: small, but the revision guard already keeps the prior state.
- (f) one config form every harness reads: the VS Code route exists because MCP is blocked there.
- (g) a design record as a pasteable URL or MCP resource: left open since September.
- (h) a reviewer model and P0 to P3 verdicts: the harness's job, a non-goal for reflow2.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-13: "anything we can learn from https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi").

WHAT IT IS, read from its README on 2026-10-13 (the README only; nothing was run or measured, and its numbers are its own claims). OMP is a fork of Mario Zechner's Pi agent, rebuilt as a terminal coding agent: about 80,000 lines of Rust for search, shell, AST, PTY and edits, plus TypeScript for the agent logic.
- It serves 31 built-in tools across files and search, runtime, code intelligence, coordination, desktop and web, and memory.
- It has its own agent-curated memory (retain, recall, reflect, learn, checkpoint, rewind), with pluggable backends.
- It runs first-class parallel subagents, each in its own worktree, plus deterministic multi-subagent workflows.
- A second model reviews every turn as an advisor.
- "Hashline" edits anchor by content hash rather than verbatim lines; the README claims 61% fewer output tokens.
- "Stream rules" inject a correction mid-stream only when the model goes off script, so they cost no standing context.
- It reads other harnesses' configs natively (.claude, .cursor, Copilot), MCP servers included.
- It has internal URL schemes (pr://, agent://, skill://), a preview-then-accept flow, and an RPC mode (NDJSON over stdio), a one-shot mode and an SDK.

THE FRAME: OMP is a harness, the model's hands. reflow2 is the graph partner. By rule:reflow2-is-one-of-three-parts-and-does-not-compete-with-the-others, most of OMP is the AI partner's side and is NOT for reflow2 to copy. The lessons are where its choices bear on the seams.

IDEAS, none chosen:
(a) THE TOOL COUNT. A full coding agent covers files, runtime, code intelligence, web, desktop and memory with 31 tools, while reflow2 serves 197. This is evidence for the already-accepted pruning (dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set): fewer, broader tools with modes. Counter: reflow2's typed tools carry the design vocabulary that stops mis-filing, and collapsing them into a few generic writes moves that vocabulary into prose the model must hold. Large: a release per step, and MCP changes must stay additive for Alex.
(b) HARNESSES NOW KEEP THEIR OWN MEMORY. OMP's retain and recall are personal, untyped agent memory. reflow2's case has to rest on what that memory is not: shared between people and models, typed and linked, authoritative (whose word), checkable (drift, gates), and surviving any one harness. Say so on the site and in the served instructions. A variant: offer reflow2 as one of OMP's memory backends. Counter: a retain/recall interface would flatten a design into facts, which is the "model absorbing the graph" failure the partnership rule names. Cheap as words; the backend is a separate, larger idea.
(c) INJECT A RULE WHEN IT IS BROKEN, NOT ON EVERY CALL. OMP's stream rules fire only on a violation. reflow2 serves lessons on tool descriptions and beside skills on every call, which costs standing context; this morning's brainstorm (b) named that cost. reflow2 cannot see the stream, but a tool reply can carry a lesson only when the call trips it (req:the-reminder-rides-the-response, still proposed). Moderate: needs a per-lesson trigger.
(d) PARALLEL SUBAGENTS ARE THE HARNESS DEFAULT NOW. Each works in its own worktree, which makes reflow2's per-agent identity and claims load-bearing (req:every-agent-working-a-design-is-its-own-claimant-subagents-included, accepted, nothing delivers it). That is emphasis, not a new idea: it raises the priority of something already accepted.
(e) HASH-ANCHORED EDITS. reflow2's replace_text already avoids re-sending a field, and every write carries a prior content hash. An edit could name the hash it expects, refusing if the node moved (compare-and-swap), so two parallel agents never overwrite each other silently. Small. Counter: the revision guard already preserves the prior state, so the gain is only an early refusal instead of a recoverable overwrite.
(f) READ OTHER HARNESSES' CONFIGS, AND WRITE ONE THING THEY ALL READ. OMP inherits .claude, .cursor and Copilot settings. If harnesses converge on reading one another's files (AGENTS.md and Agent Skills), reflow2's init could write that one form and drop per-harness adapters: via negativa on the setup paths. Counter: the VS Code route exists because MCP is blocked there, not because of config format, so one adapter stays whatever converges.
(g) A DESIGN NODE AS A URL (design://<graph_id>/<node_id>, readable as an MCP resource), as OMP serves pr:// and skill://. A link a person or agent can paste. Counter: MCP resources were weighed for flo2 in September and left open (the MCP-resources choice); a resource list over 7,000 nodes is its own cost.
(h) A SECOND MODEL AS ADVISOR, AND PARALLEL REVIEWERS WITH P0–P3 VERDICTS. That is the harness's job. reflow2's part is to be what the reviewer checks against, and to keep the verdicts as findings linked to what they judge. Nothing new to build; record_finding exists.

RANKING (a finding, not a decision): (d) costs nothing but priority. (b) is words. (e) is small. (c) and (g) are moderate. (f) and (a) are large, and (a) is already accepted intent that this only strengthens. (h) is a non-goal for reflow2.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO THE WHOLE: OMP's claims are read, not measured, and a harness's feature list changes monthly. Copying any of it would chase the AI partner's job. The durable lessons are (a), (b), (c) and (d), because they are about the seams, not features.
